description:
We are a small team of engineering students developing ARES, an autonomous rover inspired by planetary exploration. Our goal is to build a functional prototype while learning about robotics, AI, and autonomous navigation.

We welcome motivated individuals interested in programming, electronics, mechanical design, or robotics. No previous experience is required, just curiosity, teamwork, and a willingness to learn.
summary:
We are ASTRAEUS TEAM, a team of three engineering students who set out to design Mark 4 – MARS ROVER EXPLORATIO, a low-cost exploration rover built through innovation, persistence, and teamwork.

We developed a four-wheel-drive rover with an active steering system that allows each wheel to rotate ±90°. This enables crab-like lateral movement, giving the rover greater maneuverability and allowing it to evade obstacles without losing its direction of travel.

Alongside the physical design, we created a digital twin using ROS 2 and Gazebo to simulate, validate, and optimize the rover before manufacturing. Our approach combines parametric CAD, 3D printing, affordable components, and custom simulation tools to create a platform that is accessible, reproducible, and adaptable.

We believe exploration technology should not be limited by cost. Mark 4 is our effort to make advanced rover development more accessible for education, research, and future exploration missions.
details:
Mark 4 Rover

We developed Mark 4, a four-wheel-drive exploration rover featuring a rocker suspension coupled by a differential and our own active steering system. Each wheel station can rotate ±90° using an MG995 servo, allowing the rover to steer in place and move beyond conventional differential steering.

The mechanical system was fully designed in SolidWorks, using parametric sketches and commercially available M3/M5 hardware. The main components are designed for 3D printing, making the rover accessible and easy to reproduce.

Digital Twin & Simulation

We also developed a complete digital twin using ROS 2 Jazzy, Gazebo Harmonic, and Ubuntu 24.04. The model consists of 14 links and 13 joints, with multiple configurations for active steering, rocker movement, and differential behavior.

We implemented custom Python tools to calculate STL mesh inertia and validate the rover's kinematic structure, ensuring consistency between the CAD model and simulation.

Impact & Innovation

Our approach allows teams to simulate, validate, and optimize the rover before manufacturing, reducing material costs and development time. The result is a low-cost, documented, and reproducible model for learning, research, and exploration prototyping.

We focused on practical engineering details such as mechanical interference, assembly accessibility, servo alignment, reusable components, and strict CAD-to-simulation consistency.
